references.text: God tells Moses that he will send him to Pharaoh's son, which can be seen as a parallel to how God later sends his own Son.
The verse about the stone that the builders rejected, which became the cornerstone, can be interpreted as a prediction of Jesus' rejection and ultimate victory.
The prophecy about a vineyard that the Lord tends but which does not bear good fruit can be seen as a precursor to Jesus' parable.
The parable of the vineyard workers who kill the son is a direct parallel to Jesus' parable in Matthew.
Jesus' parable about the vineyard and the branches that must bear fruit can be viewed in light of his earlier parables about the vineyard.
